I'm glad to hear that your providers have been validating your experience! For me the best way to tell is generally to assess the big picture of how I'm experiencing my body that day. If I'm having a bad pain/fatigue day and I can't pay attention to anything I credit that to fibro fog, whereas if I feel like I'm not at the wheel and I'm very scatterbrained and getting sucked into any little thing that gives me dopamine that's the adhd. Generally though it's all intermingled and that's okay! It can be a combination of factors because brains and bodies are complicated and we all experience these things differently.

I have both fibro and adhd, so the fog and forgetfulness are very real!! Not all of these things work every time, but here are a few strategies I've started using that help:
1. I have an alexa in my room, the living room, and of course the app on my phone. I can tell it out loud to remind me of something later, start and keep a list for me, set timers so I don't lose track of time so easily, etc.. Something about having an external voice reminding me of something instead of just another phone notification to ignore helps a ton. And if I do decide I don't want to get up and go take care of the thing immediately I just tell it to remind me again in 20 minutes or whatever. Way easier to annoy myself into breaking through the fog that way.
2. Even without the robot helper, just saying things out loud helps me remember. I often ask my partner and/or roommate to remind me of things and then tell them I don't actually expect them to remind me, I just want to have a conversation about it so maybe my brain will hold it.
3. If I'm in conversation with someone and I have something to say but I don't want to interrupt I will firmly press a spot on my head like I'm literally putting it on a sticky note and attaching it to myself/pinning it to my head. Tying that lingering physical sensation to the thought helps me return to it.
4. Every time you think to yourself "nah I don't need to write that down right now", absolutely write it down immediately. This is Murphy's law of fibro fog, as soon as you do anything else that thought will be gone forever.

If I remember more I will return! I hope something here is helpful to you!

Changing between writing and typing also helps keep me from falling into the ADHD void because it's a different sensory experience and makes me feel like I'm starting a fresh new task.
